correctness.rationale: Substituting once at depth j gives W_{j+1}=W_j 0^{r q^j} W_j. The two copies start/end in 1, so the runs do not merge, and the new run is strictly longer than every earlier run. Thus in B_j each proper suffix either starts in 1 or has fewer leading zeros than B_j; W_0=1 handles j=0. The B_j are Lyndon and strictly decrease, so finite CFL uniqueness identifies the entire list, including k=0. The finite lists stabilize and give the infinite decomposition. In fact a Lyndon factor cannot cross a new record-run boundary from an earlier start: its suffix at the boundary is either a shorter all-zero prefix or has more leading zeros, and is smaller. An infinite Lyndon tail is also impossible because every suffix has a smaller later suffix starting at a longer run. Starts are |W_j|. Summing the linear recurrence gives n_j=2^j+r sum_{i=0}^{j-1}2^{j-1-i}q^i, with the empty sum at j=0, and generating function (1+(r-q)z)/((1-2z)(1-qz)). The two growth laws and q-uniform identity follow. The Duval checker is bounded corroboration by design and was inspected, not run.
